title: JSON mode robustness orchestration and compatibility matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a comprehensive, reproducible test orchestration and compatibility matrix for JSON mode enforcement and constrained-decoding across runtime variants and model families. This ticket drives the test design, data generation, CI integration, and rollout plan so downstream regressions in schema adherence or streaming reassembly are detected early.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestration harness can run the full matrix against at least 3 runtime releases and 4 model variants (open and quantized) with a single command
Schema adherence pass rate >= 98% on constrained-decoding acceptance tests; failures produce a structured failure artifact (reason, token stream, cursor position)
Streaming partial-chunk reconstruction tests show no data loss for out-of-order or truncated segments in >= 2000 randomized scenarios
Compatibility matrix results are uploaded to the console test-dashboard and linked in PRs; CI blocks merges on regressions against baseline (allowing documented intentional relaxations)
Fallback policy test: when strict enforcement is disabled, the runtime logs a clear deprecation/compatibility event and the output remains parseable by lenient decoders
test_cases: TC-01: Strict-schema pass/fail with constrained-decoding: feed 500 prompt+schema pairs with edge enums and missing-optional fields; verify decoder rejects invalid tokens and returns structured error
TC-02: Streaming-interleaved tooling: simulate tool-call tokens emitted mid-stream, then resume normal JSON output; verify consumer can reassemble and map tool-call boundaries
TC-03: Partial-chunk fuzzing: generate truncated streaming payloads at random byte offsets; ensure reassembly routine retries and either recovers or produces deterministic error codes
TC-04: Sampling-noise tolerance: run constrained-decoder with temperature sweep (0.0, 0.3, 0.7) and check for reproducible schema violations at higher temps
TC-05: Model-variant compatibility: run same prompt-set on float16, int8-quant, and 4-bit quantized variants; compare parse-success and produce delta report
TC-06: Backwards compatibility: verify older client SDKs using legacy streaming wire format can still parse outputs when runtime upgrades introduce schema metadata headers
TC-07: Canary rollback test: simulate a bad model rollout that increases schema violations; assert that automatic fallback to previous variant is triggered and logged within SLA
run_plan: Harness is implemented as an executable python runner (tests/run_jsonmode_matrix.py). It accepts parameters: --runtime=, --models=, --seed=, --cases=, --upload-results. The runner produces per-case JSONL artifacts and an aggregated CSV with metrics. CI job will invoke with baseline runtimes and compare to stored golden metrics; diffs above thresholds open ENG regression alerts.
notes: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting. Agreed to target 3 runtime releases (current, -1, -2) and include both hosted and dedicated-simulated environments.
2025-01-18: Data team delivered 600 diverse prompt/schema pairs derived from real QA and codegen flows. Removed duplicates and added edge-case enums.
2025-01-28: Found an edge case where KV-cache warmed prefix causes off-by-one in token offsets; added TC-03 variant to exercise prefix lengths > 2048 tokens.
2025-02-04: Design review feedback from PM (Katherine Liu): add explicit telemetry keys for 'schema_violation_type' and 'stream_reassembly_latency' to aid postmortems.
2025-02-10: Implemented upload to console test-dashboard and initial CI config; next is documenting rollout guardrails and alert thresholds.
